prompt: Why does the C=O of cyclopentanone (five-membered ring ketone) appear at ~1745 cm⁻¹, HIGHER than acetone (1715)?

options.label: Ring strain increases s-character of the C=O carbon, stiffening the C=O bond and raising its force constant.
Cyclopentanone is more polar than acetone, so dipole-dipole shifts the stretch upward.
The ring restricts resonance delocalization of the C=O, making it a stronger double bond.
The ring lowers the reduced mass of the C=O oscillator, pushing the frequency higher.

explanation: Smaller rings compress the internal C–C–C angle at the carbonyl C, forcing more s-character into the C=O bond → stiffer bond → higher ν. Trend: cyclohexanone 1715, cyclopentanone 1745, cyclobutanone 1780, cyclopropanone 1815. Reduced mass is identical across ring sizes.
